speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where in your groin you are feeling pain, and are you able to bear any weight on your right leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned pain in both knees, but I need to assess the leg positioning you described. Is your right leg externally rotated and shortened compared to the left side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positioning of your leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is highly characteristic of a posterior hip dislocation. I need to confirm the extent of the injury and check for associated fractures.
